title: RelayLLM: Efficient Reasoning via Collaborative Decoding
text: 2 , we consider a hybrid inference setting involving a primary, resource-efficient Small Language Model (SLM), denoted as ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} , and a powerful but computationally expensive Large Language Model (LLM), denoted as ℳ L \mathcal{M}_{L} . Given an input query 𝐱 \mathbf{x} , the system aims to generate a high-quality response 𝐲 \mathbf{y} through dynamic collaboration. Different from standard cascading methods that simply offload the entire remaining task to a larger model, we define an interleaved generation process where the small model acts as both reasoner and central controller. The process operates as follows: By default, ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} generates tokens autoregressively based on the current context history as a normal language model. ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} is augmented with a special control capability: it can actively request assistance by generating a specific command pattern: where ⊕ \oplus denotes string concatenation, and n ∈ ℤ + n\in\mathbb{Z}^{+} represents the number of tokens required from the larger language model. When this trigger pattern is detected, the generation by ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} pauses. The current context (including query and tokens generated by SLM) is forwarded to ℳ L \mathcal{M}_{L} . Crucially, to maintain compatibility with the large model’s standard input distribution, we strip the special command tokens ( 𝒞 cmd \mathcal{C}_{\text{cmd}} ) from the context provided to ℳ L \mathcal{M}_{L} .
